entries.literal: "The range had been increasing every day, and it ended up taking away a third of Japan's population. The other real Sekimeiya was still refrigerated, so no world switch occurred. Given that the people who vanished didn't reappear anywhere, which Sekimeiya was activated? Did everyone go to the past or to the future?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: If they had gone millennia to the past, they would never have been able to exist in the future location, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere. If they had gone millennia to the future, they wouldn't have existed in the proportional past, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere.
entries.literal: "If they had gone millennia to the past, they would never have been able to exist in the future location, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere. If they had gone millennia to the future, they wouldn't have existed in the proportional past, so they wouldn't have appeared anywhere."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Calliants are the flowers that compose the flora of Airun's base. That is what this chapter is.
entries.literal: "Calliants are the flowers that compose the flora of Airun's base. That is what this chapter is."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The base of the mountain, which lets it build all the way to the peak. In addition, this chapter is more grounded than the others.
entries.literal: "The base of the mountain, which lets it build all the way to the peak. In addition, this chapter is more grounded than the others."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Even though it's based on a real flower that can be found on snowy mountains, "calliant" is a made-up word.
entries.literal: "Even though it's based on a real flower that can be found on snowy mountains, \"calliant\" is a made-up word."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. ...Why, though?
entries.literal: "When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. ...Why, though?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This is one of the clearest indications of an elusive rule of the Sekimeiya.
entries.literal: "This is one of the clearest indications of an elusive rule of the Sekimeiya."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When someone traveled to the past, they were unable to keep feeling the pain of the burn they had noticed for an instant. The difference in Isla's case is the amount of time she traveled to the past.
entries.literal: "When someone traveled to the past, they were unable to keep feeling the pain of the burn they had noticed for an instant. The difference in Isla's case is the amount of time she traveled to the past."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When she touched it, the Past Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so normally, a painful burn would've remained on her skin. The amount of days that it took her to reach January 5th from November 24th would not have gotten rid of it. That's why she appeared with it in the first place.
entries.literal: "When she touched it, the Past Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so normally, a painful burn would've remained on her skin. The amount of days that it took her to reach January 5th from November 24th would not have gotten rid of it. That's why she appeared with it in the first place."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In other words, the body she appeared in was that of one loop of her travel.
entries.literal: "In other words, the body she appeared in was that of one loop of her travel."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When she reached January 5th, the burn she'd appeared with had healed considerably, but it was still visible. If that body of hers had been the one to appear on November 24th, an instant chain of infinite loops would've made it impossible for her burn to ever appear.
entries.literal: "When she reached January 5th, the burn she'd appeared with had healed considerably, but it was still visible. If that body of hers had been the one to appear on November 24th, an instant chain of infinite loops would've made it impossible for her burn to ever appear."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Of course, that also means that she would've died instantly; she would've aged more than a month per loop and been unable to appear in November.
entries.literal: "Of course, that also means that she would've died instantly; she would've aged more than a month per loop and been unable to appear in November."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Instead, she appeared in a body that had undergone a single loop. This behavior can be observed in a number of travels, and it's the answer behind one of the toughest questions Atsuki will face.
entries.literal: "Instead, she appeared in a body that had undergone a single loop. This behavior can be observed in a number of travels, and it's the answer behind one of the toughest questions Atsuki will face."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Why does Atsuki's injury disappear when he travels forty minutes to the past? That's not what happened the last time he traveled back in time after getting injured.
entries.literal: "Why does Atsuki's injury disappear when he travels forty minutes to the past? That's not what happened the last time he traveled back in time after getting injured."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The first reason is the amount of time it will take him to reach the future location. Even though it's minutes away, many weeks will pass until he returns to January 5th. That amount of time, enough for the injury to heal, is what makes him appear without it.
entries.literal: "The first reason is the amount of time it will take him to reach the future location. Even though it's minutes away, many weeks will pass until he returns to January 5th. That amount of time, enough for the injury to heal, is what makes him appear without it."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: However, there's another reason why his injury disappears, and it's unrelated to the amount of time that it will take him to return to January 5th. It's the same reason he doesn't appear with a burn mark when he travels all the way to November 24th, but that will be touched on a little later.
entries.literal: "However, there's another reason why his injury disappears, and it's unrelated to the amount of time that it will take him to return to January 5th. It's the same reason he doesn't appear with a burn mark when he travels all the way to November 24th, but that will be touched on a little later."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Certain events in this story have a specific characteristic to them: their origin seems unclear.
entries.literal: "Certain events in this story have a specific characteristic to them: their origin seems unclear."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The handle of the storeroom's door has been taken off by Akaro A, but the means by which that happened are not straightforward.
entries.literal: "The handle of the storeroom's door has been taken off by Akaro A, but the means by which that happened are not straightforward."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Akaro world switched to world B, and in the attic, he was told about the existence of the secret door. Afterward, he traveled to the past and removed the handle from that door. It could be said that he was told about the existence of the door because he had removed its handle.
entries.literal: "Akaro world switched to world B, and in the attic, he was told about the existence of the secret door. Afterward, he traveled to the past and removed the handle from that door. It could be said that he was told about the existence of the door because he had removed its handle."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This is not the only instance where this seeming lack of causality takes place, so where exactly is it coming from?
entries.literal: "This is not the only instance where this seeming lack of causality takes place, so where exactly is it coming from?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In world A, Akaro knew Xyn had been outsmarted. An alarm had trapped them in the tower, and the real Sekimeiya had vanished when he had woken up. Not only that, but he thought he had killed two people in order to bring his plan to success.
entries.literal: "In world A, Akaro knew Xyn had been outsmarted. An alarm had trapped them in the tower, and the real Sekimeiya had vanished when he had woken up. Not only that, but he thought he had killed two people in order to bring his plan to success."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: He hated the way the world had turned out, but altering the reality he'd experienced wasn't possible. However, eventually, he world switched to world B.{w} Someone else originally from world A came with him: Isla.
entries.literal: "He hated the way the world had turned out, but altering the reality he'd experienced wasn't possible. However, eventually, he world switched to world B.{w} Someone else originally from world A came with him: Isla."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In world A, Isla never expected that an attack would take place in the tower. She followed the adults and hoped that everything would be resolved quickly. ...A lot of time passed, though, and at one point, her mother had been missing for a while after going to the bathroom.
entries.literal: "In world A, Isla never expected that an attack would take place in the tower. She followed the adults and hoped that everything would be resolved quickly. ...A lot of time passed, though, and at one point, her mother had been missing for a while after going to the bathroom."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Isla couldn't bring herself to voice her worry, as that would've meant admitting that something could've happened to her mother. However, she regretted the way she'd acted; she wished she could've told Erina to stay with her.
entries.literal: "Isla couldn't bring herself to voice her worry, as that would've meant admitting that something could've happened to her mother. However, she regretted the way she'd acted; she wished she could've told Erina to stay with her."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Akaro and Isla world switched to world B. As soon as they appeared in that world, they shaped it in a way they couldn't change their own.
entries.literal: "Akaro and Isla world switched to world B. As soon as they appeared in that world, they shaped it in a way they couldn't change their own."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Atsuki and Shiroya B were able to save Miiya in world C, but didn't that only happen because she had already been saved?
entries.literal: "Atsuki and Shiroya B were able to save Miiya in world C, but didn't that only happen because she had already been saved?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This behavior of the world switch defined the relationship between the three worlds, instantly shaping three drastically different sets of events.
entries.literal: "This behavior of the world switch defined the relationship between the three worlds, instantly shaping three drastically different sets of events."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: And when a two-way world switch happened, someone was pulled backward in the order of switches. In those instances, both worlds balanced each other out accordingly. By working like this, the world switches led into the progression between the three worlds.
entries.literal: "And when a two-way world switch happened, someone was pulled backward in the order of switches. In those instances, both worlds balanced each other out accordingly. By working like this, the world switches led into the progression between the three worlds."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In world A, only Atsuki made it to {time=21}, and he was accused of the murders that had taken place. Not a lot of time passed before a large portion of Japan suddenly disappeared forever.
entries.literal: "In world A, only Atsuki made it to {time=21}, and he was accused of the murders that had taken place. Not a lot of time passed before a large portion of Japan suddenly disappeared forever."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: World B was a step up, but being between worlds A and C, it was filled with many bittersweet resolutions. Despite a few deaths, some people got out safely. Isla returned, but it wasn't the Isla who had died. Akaro was arrested, but it was the Akaro who most regretted what he'd done. Atsuki and Shiroya left happily, but they would never see Miiya again.
entries.literal: "World B was a step up, but being between worlds A and C, it was filled with many bittersweet resolutions. Despite a few deaths, some people got out safely. Isla returned, but it wasn't the Isla who had died. Akaro was arrested, but it was the Akaro who most regretted what he'd done. Atsuki and Shiroya left happily, but they would never see Miiya again."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: World C existed thanks to world B. Everyone who was trapped got out alive. The people of that world faced numerous hardships, but they were all resolved. Naomi seemed to die, but she returned. Shiroya seemed to die, but she returned. Erina seemed to die, but she returned.{w} ...Then, why is it a world so close to world A?
entries.literal: "World C existed thanks to world B. Everyone who was trapped got out alive. The people of that world faced numerous hardships, but they were all resolved. Naomi seemed to die, but she returned. Shiroya seemed to die, but she returned. Erina seemed to die, but she returned.{w} ...Then, why is it a world so close to world A?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: A step was taken when world C was created, but what direction did it take? A bit more examination is needed to reach that answer.
entries.literal: "A step was taken when world C was created, but what direction did it take? A bit more examination is needed to reach that answer."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In any case, the labyrinth spawned by the world switches always operated under the inherent progression that it had created. Some people from world A ended up in world B. Some people from world B ended up in world C, but their world A selves pulled them back to world B. Some people from world C visited worlds A and B, but they were able to safely return to world C.{w} Thanks to the recording obtained in world C, Akaro A was arrested in world B. Atsuki A was the only person from his world to momentarily reach world C, but he dropped all the way back to world A when his elevator ride to the top vanished out of nowhere, the exact moment Shiroya B traveled to November to make world C the world it was...
entries.literal: "In any case, the labyrinth spawned by the world switches always operated under the inherent progression that it had created. Some people from world A ended up in world B. Some people from world B ended up in world C, but their world A selves pulled them back to world B. Some people from world C visited worlds A and B, but they were able to safely return to world C.{w} Thanks to the recording obtained in world C, Akaro A was arrested in world B. Atsuki A was the only person from his world to momentarily reach world C, but he dropped all the way back to world A when his elevator ride to the top vanished out of nowhere, the exact moment Shiroya B traveled to November to make world C the world it was..."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The labyrinth never stopped spinning, and somewhere, it hid the peak that everyone wanted to reach. There's only one place where it would not have moved.
entries.literal: "The labyrinth never stopped spinning, and somewhere, it hid the peak that everyone wanted to reach. There's only one place where it would not have moved."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: I hope you had enough time to think about this mystery.{w} As you might have guessed, the Past Sekimeiya was involved.
entries.literal: "I hope you had enough time to think about this mystery.{w} As you might have guessed, the Past Sekimeiya was involved."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Sai traveled to the past and appeared in the locked elevator. Before asking "why", though, it's necessary to ask "how". Without the Sekimeiya, in the future location of Sai's travel, he wouldn't have been able to enter the elevator. Hence, traveling to the past and appearing inside it seems impossible.
entries.literal: "Sai traveled to the past and appeared in the locked elevator. Before asking \"why\", though, it's necessary to ask \"how\". Without the Sekimeiya, in the future location of Sai's travel, he wouldn't have been able to enter the elevator. Hence, traveling to the past and appearing inside it seems impossible."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: As long as the past and future states align and the events in between are possible, many elaborate setups can be created.
entries.literal: "As long as the past and future states align and the events in between are possible, many elaborate setups can be created."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Consider this chart depicting one of Sai's possible journeys. Atsuki and Shiroya have trapped themselves in the elevator.
entries.literal: "Consider this chart depicting one of Sai's possible journeys. Atsuki and Shiroya have trapped themselves in the elevator."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Sai thinks about his next course of action and decides to use the Past Sekimeiya. After allowing it to warm up, he touches it.{w} But how is his past position determined?
entries.literal: "Sai thinks about his next course of action and decides to use the Past Sekimeiya. After allowing it to warm up, he touches it.{w} But how is his past position determined?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The answer is that he continues to live virtually, as if he did not time travel. Movements during this time can be natural or driven with clear intent. Let's say he virtually moves until he reaches room B4.
entries.literal: "The answer is that he continues to live virtually, as if he did not time travel. Movements during this time can be natural or driven with clear intent. Let's say he virtually moves until he reaches room B4."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When he arrives in the past, he will be in room B4. Right now, this new timeline is imaginary. It will become real once the past state matches the future state.
entries.literal: "When he arrives in the past, he will be in room B4. Right now, this new timeline is imaginary. It will become real once the past state matches the future state."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Next, he takes out the Past Sekimeiya and allows it to warm up. He touches it and lives virtually until he reaches the floor 4 partitions.
entries.literal: "Next, he takes out the Past Sekimeiya and allows it to warm up. He touches it and lives virtually until he reaches the floor 4 partitions."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: What's important is that the new timeline does not prevent the first travel from occurring.
entries.literal: "What's important is that the new timeline does not prevent the first travel from occurring."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This means that the Past Sekimeiya must be in the same location and charge state as it was when the first travel happened.
entries.literal: "This means that the Past Sekimeiya must be in the same location and charge state as it was when the first travel happened."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This travel creates another imaginary timeline, and Sai now exists before the elevator is stopped.
entries.literal: "This travel creates another imaginary timeline, and Sai now exists before the elevator is stopped."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Taking this opportunity, he enters it and traps himself between floors.
entries.literal: "Taking this opportunity, he enters it and traps himself between floors."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Isn't this a contradiction, though? In the real timeline, Atsuki and Shiroya are in the elevator, but here, Sai is alone.
entries.literal: "Isn't this a contradiction, though? In the real timeline, Atsuki and Shiroya are in the elevator, but here, Sai is alone."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Try thinking about what the original Sai sees and hears from his perspective. As long as the circumstances that allowed the first travel to happen are preserved, this is valid.
entries.literal: "Try thinking about what the original Sai sees and hears from his perspective. As long as the circumstances that allowed the first travel to happen are preserved, this is valid."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In any case, this is the power of virtual timelines. The absurdities will soon collapse into a single truth.
entries.literal: "In any case, this is the power of virtual timelines. The absurdities will soon collapse into a single truth."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Notice that the future position of the third timeline no longer matches the second. Sai can no longer go to the 4th floor partitions since he's stuck in the elevator.
entries.literal: "Notice that the future position of the third timeline no longer matches the second. Sai can no longer go to the 4th floor partitions since he's stuck in the elevator."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The result is that the future position in the second timeline is updated to match the third. The past position in the third timeline is updated accordingly.
entries.literal: "The result is that the future position in the second timeline is updated to match the third. The past position in the third timeline is updated accordingly."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In this latest iteration of the third timeline, Sai appears midair inside the elevator and crashes down. He repeats the process of trapping himself between floors.
entries.literal: "In this latest iteration of the third timeline, Sai appears midair inside the elevator and crashes down. He repeats the process of trapping himself between floors."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The validity of the third timeline is preserved, so let's see what happens if we look farther into the future.
entries.literal: "The validity of the third timeline is preserved, so let's see what happens if we look farther into the future."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The future position of the first timeline is updated to be in the elevator, which updates the past position in the second timeline.
entries.literal: "The future position of the first timeline is updated to be in the elevator, which updates the past position in the second timeline."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: However, this raises an issue.
entries.literal: "However, this raises an issue."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Sai can no longer perform the second travel since now he appears in the stopped elevator.
entries.literal: "Sai can no longer perform the second travel since now he appears in the stopped elevator."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This destroys the third timeline, but preserves its effect.{w} The future position in the first timeline is inside the elevator after it closed.
entries.literal: "This destroys the third timeline, but preserves its effect.{w} The future position in the first timeline is inside the elevator after it closed."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: After killing Atsuki and Shiroya, Sai's past and future positions finally match. The virtual timeline stabilizes and becomes reality.
entries.literal: "After killing Atsuki and Shiroya, Sai's past and future positions finally match. The virtual timeline stabilizes and becomes reality."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Perhaps you don't like the idea that Atsuki and Shiroya aren't in the elevator in the third timeline.
entries.literal: "Perhaps you don't like the idea that Atsuki and Shiroya aren't in the elevator in the third timeline."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: That's fine. This merely demonstrates the concept.
entries.literal: "That's fine. This merely demonstrates the concept."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Another method might involve Sai falling down the elevator shaft in a virtual timeline and entering the elevator from the top.
entries.literal: "Another method might involve Sai falling down the elevator shaft in a virtual timeline and entering the elevator from the top."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: As long as the goal is achievable within the travel and the user has the will to reach it, the Past Sekimeiya will turn it into reality.
entries.literal: "As long as the goal is achievable within the travel and the user has the will to reach it, the Past Sekimeiya will turn it into reality."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The key is to set the future state to be within the elevator. The exact method is not important as long as there is at least one valid option in the sea of possibilities.
entries.literal: "The key is to set the future state to be within the elevator. The exact method is not important as long as there is at least one valid option in the sea of possibilities."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The concept of virtual timelines and iterative updates can be found elsewhere in the story. I wonder what solutions you'll come up with.
entries.literal: "The concept of virtual timelines and iterative updates can be found elsewhere in the story. I wonder what solutions you'll come up with."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Atsuki obtains an equation for the Sekimeiya's travel times using hypothetical worlds. We'll call these "virtual worlds".
entries.literal: "Atsuki obtains an equation for the Sekimeiya's travel times using hypothetical worlds. We'll call these \"virtual worlds\"."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Through countless iterations, he uses his virtual selves to produce a result that's observed in the real world.
entries.literal: "Through countless iterations, he uses his virtual selves to produce a result that's observed in the real world."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: While this concept works for him, Atsuki isn't aware of how lucky he is to formulate the plan the way he does.
entries.literal: "While this concept works for him, Atsuki isn't aware of how lucky he is to formulate the plan the way he does."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Let's take a look at a simple travel using the Past Sekimeiya. In this example, we'll pay close attention to the age of the user throughout the sequence. The node {b}t{/b} represents the moment at which the Sekimeiya is activated.
entries.literal: "Let's take a look at a simple travel using the Past Sekimeiya. In this example, we'll pay close attention to the age of the user throughout the sequence. The node {b}t{/b} represents the moment at which the Sekimeiya is activated."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The Sekimeiya sends the user twenty minutes back in time. In order to determine the user's state in the past, a virtual copy of the user is created that continues to live as if they had not time traveled. After twenty minutes, their final state is used in the past.
entries.literal: "The Sekimeiya sends the user twenty minutes back in time. In order to determine the user's state in the past, a virtual copy of the user is created that continues to live as if they had not time traveled. After twenty minutes, their final state is used in the past."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Both past and future locations are equidistant from the travel point, which means that in this virtual world, the user will arrive in the past being twenty minutes older than at the moment the Sekimeiya was activated.
entries.literal: "Both past and future locations are equidistant from the travel point, which means that in this virtual world, the user will arrive in the past being twenty minutes older than at the moment the Sekimeiya was activated."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: And when the user makes it to the future copy point of the second virtual world, they will be sixty minutes older than at the moment of the travel.
entries.literal: "And when the user makes it to the future copy point of the second virtual world, they will be sixty minutes older than at the moment of the travel."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: In this second world, the user is able to update their future state.
entries.literal: "In this second world, the user is able to update their future state."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The state {b}t+20{/b} does not account for the user's behavior in the past, but {b}t+60{/b} does. This update stage is essential for convergence.
entries.literal: "The state {b}t+20{/b} does not account for the user's behavior in the past, but {b}t+60{/b} does. This update stage is essential for convergence."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The next step is a third virtual world.
entries.literal: "The next step is a third virtual world."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Since the previous stage's final position is copied, the user will age by another forty minutes and will be 100 minutes older at the end of the travel.
entries.literal: "Since the previous stage's final position is copied, the user will age by another forty minutes and will be 100 minutes older at the end of the travel."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This stage exists to confirm the loop is stable. The user must have identical positions and possessions at {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b}. The ages of the body and possessions will be slightly older, but everything else is identical.
entries.literal: "This stage exists to confirm the loop is stable. The user must have identical positions and possessions at {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b}. The ages of the body and possessions will be slightly older, but everything else is identical."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: If the most recent virtual world was stable, the next step will apply the final result to the real world.
entries.literal: "If the most recent virtual world was stable, the next step will apply the final result to the real world."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When the user appears in the past, they are sixty minutes older than the moment they touched the Sekimeiya, and in the copy point of the future, they will be 100 minutes older. When a user reaches the future state in reality, they have experienced five times the travel time.
entries.literal: "When the user appears in the past, they are sixty minutes older than the moment they touched the Sekimeiya, and in the copy point of the future, they will be 100 minutes older. When a user reaches the future state in reality, they have experienced five times the travel time."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: This is how infinite aging is avoided. The update stage is required to account for the user's actions in the past, and the final stable loop is frozen and applied to reality. Of course, every stage starts with the memories from the {b}t{/b} point.
entries.literal: "This is how infinite aging is avoided. The update stage is required to account for the user's actions in the past, and the final stable loop is frozen and applied to reality. Of course, every stage starts with the memories from the {b}t{/b} point."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: A clear example of this kind of sequence is Isla's burn. Touching the Sekimeiya left a burn scar on her finger that this system didn't have enough time to erase. Naturally, however, she didn't age infinitely.
entries.literal: "A clear example of this kind of sequence is Isla's burn. Touching the Sekimeiya left a burn scar on her finger that this system didn't have enough time to erase. Naturally, however, she didn't age infinitely."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Atsuki is able to successfully execute his plan, but he's not fully aware of how the Past Sekimeiya works. His understanding is that Sai's watch displayed the year 9,999 through infinite virtual loops.
entries.literal: "Atsuki is able to successfully execute his plan, but he's not fully aware of how the Past Sekimeiya works. His understanding is that Sai's watch displayed the year 9,999 through infinite virtual loops."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: However, that's incorrect. If the loops operated like that, Sai would have instantly died in the process, and the watch would've disintegrated.
entries.literal: "However, that's incorrect. If the loops operated like that, Sai would have instantly died in the process, and the watch would've disintegrated."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: So let's consider a different way Atsuki could have formulated his plan.
entries.literal: "So let's consider a different way Atsuki could have formulated his plan."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past and appear in the hallway holding a notepad. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things."
entries.literal: "\"If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past and appear in the hallway holding a notepad. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "1: If it has a formula written down, forty minutes later, I'll be holding it, so that's how I will have appeared with it."
entries.literal: "\"1: If it has a formula written down, forty minutes later, I'll be holding it, so that's how I will have appeared with it.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "2: If I don't appear with a notepad, by using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start working toward finding the formula. Before forty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a "1" along with the progress I made in those forty minutes. In the future location, I'll be holding the notepad."
entries.literal: "\"2: If I don't appear with a notepad, by using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start working toward finding the formula. Before forty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a \"1\" along with the progress I made in those forty minutes. In the future location, I'll be holding the notepad.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} Using the information in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the forty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and make sure that I'm holding it in the future location."
entries.literal: "\"3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} Using the information in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the forty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and make sure that I'm holding it in the future location.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The concept is almost the same as the one he actually uses, but there's a very important distinction. In this example, Atsuki doesn't get any information before he travels. Instead, he appears with a notepad after traveling to the past.
entries.literal: "The concept is almost the same as the one he actually uses, but there's a very important distinction. In this example, Atsuki doesn't get any information before he travels. Instead, he appears with a notepad after traveling to the past."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: According to what Atsuki believes at this point in time, this sequence should've worked too since it's almost identical to what he believes happened to Sai's watch. However, if he had attempted it, it would not have worked.
entries.literal: "According to what Atsuki believes at this point in time, this sequence should've worked too since it's almost identical to what he believes happened to Sai's watch. However, if he had attempted it, it would not have worked."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The reason is simple. In the virtual worlds, the location of arrival would not have changed after the update stage. The same mechanism that prevents infinite aging would've prevented the infinite information gathering system. In the real world, Atsuki could only have appeared with a notepad containing sixty minutes' worth of information.{w} Not only that, but the plan contains a glaring contradiction. Points {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b} are necessarily identical in every way except age, so appearing with a notepad that contains different information from the one that will be held in the future copy point is conceptually flawed. Even though it's what Atsuki believes happened to Sai's watch, it's fundamentally faulty, as it breaks the rule that past and future points must be identical.
entries.literal: "The reason is simple. In the virtual worlds, the location of arrival would not have changed after the update stage. The same mechanism that prevents infinite aging would've prevented the infinite information gathering system. In the real world, Atsuki could only have appeared with a notepad containing sixty minutes' worth of information.{w} Not only that, but the plan contains a glaring contradiction. Points {b}t+60{/b} and {b}t+100{/b} are necessarily identical in every way except age, so appearing with a notepad that contains different information from the one that will be held in the future copy point is conceptually flawed. Even though it's what Atsuki believes happened to Sai's watch, it's fundamentally faulty, as it breaks the rule that past and future points must be identical."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: ...So why did his original plan work? Where's the loophole that allows him to manifest this infinitely iterated information without aging infinitely?
entries.literal: "...So why did his original plan work? Where's the loophole that allows him to manifest this infinitely iterated information without aging infinitely?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Let's refresh our memory on the method through which Atsuki obtains the Sekimeiya's formula.
entries.literal: "Let's refresh our memory on the method through which Atsuki obtains the Sekimeiya's formula."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past.{w} But before I touch it, I'll open the door to the hallway and find a notepad from the bedrooms on the floor. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things."
entries.literal: "\"If I touch the Sekimeiya when fifteen minutes have passed, I'll go twenty minutes to the past.{w} But before I touch it, I'll open the door to the hallway and find a notepad from the bedrooms on the floor. Depending on what it says, I'll do one of three things.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "1: If it has a formula written down, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, obtain the notepad, write the formula down, and leave it in the hallway."
entries.literal: "\"1: If it has a formula written down, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, obtain the notepad, write the formula down, and leave it in the hallway.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "2: If I don't find a notepad, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, and using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start to work toward finding the formula. Before twenty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a "1" along with the progress I made in those twenty minutes. Then, I'll leave it in the hallway."
entries.literal: "\"2: If I don't find a notepad, I'll go twenty minutes to the past, and using the Future Sekimeiya in the kitchen, I'll start to work toward finding the formula. Before twenty minutes pass, I'll obtain a notepad from the bedrooms, and in the top left corner of the first page, I'll write a \"1\" along with the progress I made in those twenty minutes. Then, I'll leave it in the hallway.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: "3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} I'll go back to the past, and using the information I read in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the twenty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and then leave the notepad in the hallway."
entries.literal: "\"3: If I find a notepad that doesn't contain the formula, it will have my current progress along with a number in the top left corner of the first page, which will indicate the amount of iterations that have occurred so far.{w} I'll go back to the past, and using the information I read in the notepad, I'll start working to find the formula. Before the twenty minutes pass, I'll write down the updated progress in a notepad from the bedrooms, increase the number I saw in the top left corner by one, and then leave the notepad in the hallway.\""

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: As you might've noticed, the reason behind his success lies in observing the information left by the virtual worlds before touching the Sekimeiya.
entries.literal: "As you might've noticed, the reason behind his success lies in observing the information left by the virtual worlds before touching the Sekimeiya."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The Atsukis in the virtual worlds leave the notepad in the hallway so that the Atsuki before the {b}t{/b} point can see it. In other words, stage 2 feeds information to stage 1.
entries.literal: "The Atsukis in the virtual worlds leave the notepad in the hallway so that the Atsuki before the {b}t{/b} point can see it. In other words, stage 2 feeds information to stage 1."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: That causes {b}t{/b}'s starting memories to continuously update, and the calculations made at the {b}t+60{/b} point are no longer locked to a state of a single round of calculations.
entries.literal: "That causes {b}t{/b}'s starting memories to continuously update, and the calculations made at the {b}t+60{/b} point are no longer locked to a state of a single round of calculations."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When the sequence converges and the final result is applied to the real world, Atsuki appears in the past having aged only sixty minutes but having spent infinite time computing. This is thanks to the virtual worlds continuously updating the starting point through real Atsuki's memories.
entries.literal: "When the sequence converges and the final result is applied to the real world, Atsuki appears in the past having aged only sixty minutes but having spent infinite time computing. This is thanks to the virtual worlds continuously updating the starting point through real Atsuki's memories."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. The Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so the burn would not have faded by the time the future location took place.
entries.literal: "When Isla A traveled from December 15th to November 24th, she appeared with a burn mark on her finger. The Sekimeiya was immensely hot, so the burn would not have faded by the time the future location took place."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: So then, why does Atsuki not appear with a burn mark on November 24th? The Sekimeiya was about as hot, and he will spend even fewer days to reach the future position since he will travel forward in time from December 15th to January 5th.
entries.literal: "So then, why does Atsuki not appear with a burn mark on November 24th? The Sekimeiya was about as hot, and he will spend even fewer days to reach the future position since he will travel forward in time from December 15th to January 5th."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The answer lies in what will happen to Atsuki the night he will arrive at the motel. He will travel to the future in order to duplicate his money, but due to a miscalculation, he will replicate his body from November 24th.
entries.literal: "The answer lies in what will happen to Atsuki the night he will arrive at the motel. He will travel to the future in order to duplicate his money, but due to a miscalculation, he will replicate his body from November 24th."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: That body didn't have a burn, so he never appeared with one.
entries.literal: "That body didn't have a burn, so he never appeared with one."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The biggest reason why this loop doesn't work for Atsuki is that the box Atase took only contained the Past Sekimeiya.
entries.literal: "The biggest reason why this loop doesn't work for Atsuki is that the box Atase took only contained the Past Sekimeiya."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: While he's rushing his actions, Atsuki can't help but feel like that doesn't make sense.
entries.literal: "While he's rushing his actions, Atsuki can't help but feel like that doesn't make sense."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: He recalls that he returned to his world at {time=19:30}, which is approaching. That's why he rushes Shiroya to activate the Sekimeiya at that time and make the people in the center of the tower change worlds.
entries.literal: "He recalls that he returned to his world at {time=19:30}, which is approaching. That's why he rushes Shiroya to activate the Sekimeiya at that time and make the people in the center of the tower change worlds."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: But of course, that's slightly paradoxical. Why did the travel happen at {time=19:30} in the first place? His hurry to take this action only existed because the world switch had been lived through once, so why did it not just happen at a later point?
entries.literal: "But of course, that's slightly paradoxical. Why did the travel happen at {time=19:30} in the first place? His hurry to take this action only existed because the world switch had been lived through once, so why did it not just happen at a later point?"

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: There's something Atsuki is mistaken about. Shiroya traveling to November 30th isn't what makes everyone world switch back to world B. It is Atsuki A who causes that when he travels from world B to world C, pulling them back to their world. That's why he has no control over the time at which the world switch takes place.
entries.literal: "There's something Atsuki is mistaken about. Shiroya traveling to November 30th isn't what makes everyone world switch back to world B. It is Atsuki A who causes that when he travels from world B to world C, pulling them back to their world. That's why he has no control over the time at which the world switch takes place."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: Nonetheless, when Shiroya travels to November, she does cause a world switch. Both immense ranges still overlapped in the middle of the tower, and only one person found themselves there: Atsuki A, cluelessly taking the elevator up. Before his ride ends, Shiroya's touch makes him go back to world A, where no elevator is supporting him, and he falls onto the one below him.
entries.literal: "Nonetheless, when Shiroya travels to November, she does cause a world switch. Both immense ranges still overlapped in the middle of the tower, and only one person found themselves there: Atsuki A, cluelessly taking the elevator up. Before his ride ends, Shiroya's touch makes him go back to world A, where no elevator is supporting him, and he falls onto the one below him."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: That burning touch of the Sekimeiya was the catalyst behind the events that unfolded on December 15th. Shiroya traveled to the future and suddenly found herself in her apartment. It was December 19th, and the first thing she did was call Atsuki's phone.
entries.literal: "That burning touch of the Sekimeiya was the catalyst behind the events that unfolded on December 15th. Shiroya traveled to the future and suddenly found herself in her apartment. It was December 19th, and the first thing she did was call Atsuki's phone."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: During the twelve hours of December 15th, Atsuki B vaguely wondered something. He knew he had to make sure that Shiroya's body wouldn't be found in world C so that Miiya could be saved, but that would only work out because her body had already not been found. Atsuki wasn't sure how that detail had originated.{w} Regardless, he instructed Shiroya to keep her world C self hidden from the world. Yet, in the end, she didn't end up causing that: it was Shiroya C herself who was attracted to the Sekimeiya's glow and vanished from the world for weeks.
entries.literal: "During the twelve hours of December 15th, Atsuki B vaguely wondered something. He knew he had to make sure that Shiroya's body wouldn't be found in world C so that Miiya could be saved, but that would only work out because her body had already not been found. Atsuki wasn't sure how that detail had originated.{w} Regardless, he instructed Shiroya to keep her world C self hidden from the world. Yet, in the end, she didn't end up causing that: it was Shiroya C herself who was attracted to the Sekimeiya's glow and vanished from the world for weeks."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: The importance behind that action was even larger than Atsuki had thought. Due to Shiroya's disappearance, Akaro believed that he had killed a young girl, which developed into the attack of December 15th.
entries.literal: "The importance behind that action was even larger than Atsuki had thought. Due to Shiroya's disappearance, Akaro believed that he had killed a young girl, which developed into the attack of December 15th."

entries.speaker: c
entries.text: And although it was world C's own flow that made that happen, it was thanks to world B's influence that it occurred. Shiroya C avoided falling into a coma because her world B self shielded her while both of them fell through the floor of the gem shop.
entries.literal: "And although it was world C's own flow that made that happen, it was thanks to world B's influence that it occurred. Shiroya C avoided falling into a coma because her world B self shielded her while both of them fell through the floor of the gem shop."

entries.text:
-Ashiya Tower
In front of the event room, Atsuki touches the Sekimeiya and finds himself in the dark. Thanks to a faint light, he realizes he's in the lobby of Ashiya Tower.
While he's in hallway B, a robotic voice coming from the security room plays throughout the floor. Atsuki realizes it's not addressing him, and he rushes to the staff room, where he can't be recorded.
After a very long wait in the dark, the lights suddenly turn on.
Atsuki hears a sound in the hallway, and soon after, the door to the staff room is opened by a man carrying a black suitcase.
The man pushes Atsuki against the wall, making him rapidly lose consciousness. Before Atsuki's world fades, he sees four people in front of him, all of whom he recognizes—two men, a woman, and a girl.
Atsuki dies in a world devoid of sense—a frozen world that had defied a very important rule.
Ending: Ethereal Arc

entries.text:
-Yushibana
On the {u}29th of November{/u}, Atsuki, Shiroya, and Miiya meet up at Atsuki's house. At Miiya's suggestion, they buy three tickets for an event to be held in Ashiya Tower on December 15th, named "The Sekimeiya".
The next day, late in the evening, an explosion takes place inside a gem shop in Yushibana after a soporific gas is released inside. The impact kills Miiya instantly and makes Shiroya fall through the floor, putting her in a temporary coma.
After Shiroya reawakens, she and Atsuki live together until December 15th, when they go to Ashiya Tower early in the morning to attend the event.

entries.text:
-Yushibana
The police are waiting in front of Ashiya Tower for the shutter to unlock. Suripo hasn't been able to find Vaisude in a long time.
{u}At {time=21}{/u}, the shutter rises. Nobody is in the lobby, and the police are taken aback by the smell inside the building. Viewing the hall with an optical gas imaging camera reveals that there's an invisible gas present in the tower.
Wearing protective suits, a team of policemen rushes in. They find corpses in the security room, B4, A5, and in the men's bathroom. Above the first staircase is a girl with blue hair. Once taken outside, she reveals that her name is Shiroya.
A second policeman returns to the lobby and reports the four deaths. Nobody else was found alive, but an egg-shaped gemstone was in the attic, and it was placed in the event room's cabinet as instructed.
When two more policemen come back, one of them inquires about a movable wall found in the storeroom. Confused, they walk to the left side of the tower and make out a hidden door around the bricks. After picking the lock, they find themselves in the storeroom.
The fifth and last policeman leaves the tower. His report is the same, but he's holding a note that he found on the first floor.

entries.text:
-Yushibana
Shiroya's inaction alters the flow of events leading to this point. After touching the Sekimeiya in Ashiya Tower, Shiroya finds herself underground. Once she makes it out, she is able to roam free in Yushibana, and she ends up at her apartment.
The next day, she wakes up and decides to walk to Ina Café. When she gets there, however, she finds a note regarding its temporary shutdown.
The braking of a car startles Shiroya. When she steps to the car in the middle of the road, she finds Atsuki lying on the ground. After the police arrive on the scene, they take Shiroya away by force.
On {u}January 11th of 2012{/u}, Shiroya is released. She walks to her apartment, having heard long ago about what had happened on December 15th: nobody had been found alive in Ashiya Tower. The corpses of Naomi Cabca and Isla Majutsu had been all the police encountered within an unidentifiable gas. In January, Sai Yomiya, Akaro Esata, and Erina Majutsu were still missing.
The aftermath of the attack causes Ashiya Tower to remain closed until it is bought anonymously. Soon, it is announced that Ashiya Tower will be demolished.
On October 4th at {time=12}, the long-standing building falls down. A week later, as the debris is being cleaned, the shattered bodies of the three missing people are found deep under the rubble.     
Ending: Forsaken Relay

-Ina Café
The news on the TV says that a Xyn member was caught yesterday in Yushibana, and the screen shows an image very similar to what was in the newspaper.
I'm not able to put together a convincing theory regarding what happened, but the main takeaway is that the past was changed.
-Yushibana
I leave Ina, no longer afraid of changing history.
I decide to take Atsuki's tickets for the event, but after waiting near his house, I decide to go to Isla's first. As I'm knocking on her door, I accidentally open it and realize it isn't locked.
I find Isla's purse. Both tickets for December 15th are inside, so I quickly take them before stepping out.
-Home
I make it home and cook instant noodles. Lying on the carpet of my living room, the hours quickly pass.

-Crystal floor
I step into hallway A, filled with darkness and the same smell from the 15th. The security room is vacant, but I'm able to find the rusty key inside a drawer.
The breakers in the mechanical room are all turned on. Above them, I find the attic key and the Sekimeiya cabinet key.
-Event room
I make my way to the event room, which is colder than the rest of the building. The glass of the cabinet isn't firmly shut, and the Sekimeiya is behind it, next to a strange white substance.
I notice that the glass is cracked and stuck in place. Trying to scroll it down, I accidentally break it, triggering an alarm.
Beside the Sekimeiya, I find a card with the word "XYN" written on it. As I'm reaching my hand toward the Sekimeiya, I notice an immensely hot aura around it despite the cold of the cabinet.

-Hallway B
Lingering smoke is in the air, which makes us think we're at the {u}start of December 15th{/u}. After hearing a sound in the hallway, we're drawn to room B4.
-Crystal room B4
The cabinet where the Sekimeiya was first hidden on that day is set to 0ºC, and the temperature wheel is not broken. Atsuki lifts the cover, and we see the Sekimeiya inside the cabinet.
The Sekimeiya is burning hot, so we take it out of the cabinet and touch it, hoping to escape from the tower. When Atsuki makes contact with it, the Sekimeiya disappears, and I quickly realize that the cabinet closed without making a noise.

We hear the attic door being shut, and it's locked when we reach it. I look inside my purse and see that the attic key is still there.

entries.text:
-Ashiya Tower
While Atsuki is crying on a bed, Sai steps out of room B6, confused—the Sekimeiya disappeared without him having touched them.
As he looks through the crystal floor, he realizes it's not the place he's familiar with. The corpses he knew of have vanished, and others have appeared.
The moment Sai shows himself to Atsuki, he is welcomed by a sudden blow that comes close to ending his life. Wielding a knife, he retaliates and chases Atsuki.
Sai comes across a locked bathroom on floor 6, where Atsuki must've hidden. Aware of the location of two Sekimeiya, Sai runs to the crystal floor.
Many hours later, Atsuki is still locked up inside that bathroom. When he steps out of it, nobody is in sight.
On the crystal floor, Atsuki is drawn to the storeroom, where a glowing Sekimeiya lies in the dark. After touching it, it disappears.
Near the stairs, Erina's corpse is no longer there. When Atsuki enters the event room, he finds the Sekimeiya on the floor. Once again, the instant he touches it, it disappears.
Atsuki notices that the panel next to the elevator is properly attached and uses it to call the elevator.
{u}At {time=21:04}{/u}, the police enter the building and find the corpses of Shiroya Mirana in the lobby, Erina Majutsu near the staircase, and Sai Yomiya split in half in hallway B. The Sekimeiya cabinet is empty, but two Sekimeiya are shortly found and placed inside it.
Trying to find the missing people, a police officer inspects the elevator shaft, where Atsuki's unconscious body is found. He's taken to safety, but his account of events quickly begins to be questioned.
Many weeks after December 15th, almost a third of Japan's population disappears forever.

entries.text:
-Yushibana
On {u}November 27th{/u}, Gan, an owner of a gem shop, finds a peculiar gemstone on an unexplored mountain. Once he brings it home, he calls Ashiya with hopes of selling the discovery to them.
He quickly finds out that the gem becomes hot indoors and fears Ashiya will refuse a deal due to that.
The next day, when one of Ashiya's representatives visits the shop, Gan warns him to always keep the gemstone, named "Sekimeiya", cold.
On {u}November 29th{/u}, Gan returns to the place where he found the gemstone and finds an identical one. Back home, he calls Ashiya again, and they are also willing to take the second one despite the Sekimeiya having already been announced for showing on the 15th of December.

entries.text:
-Ashiya Tower
When the first group is brought to the event room, Katei steps out of the security room and walks to the lobby.
The smoke is released in the hallways, making everyone hurriedly evacuate. Katei uses that moment to reenter hallway A and crawls to avoid inhaling too much of the smoke.
From the hallway, Katei sees which of the two Sekimeiya Atase replaces. When Atase returns to the cleaning room, Katei takes the real Sekimeiya from the cabinet.
Katei takes the other real Sekimeiya from the cleaning cart and brings them to the security room's secret corridor, where he puts them in a suitcase he had left there.
As he's about to unlock the secret exit, Katei realizes he dropped the key while he was crawling. He returns to hallway A and is able to find it near the event room.
Even with the key, Katei isn't able to unlock the door in the storeroom. After lamenting his defeat, he realizes the suitcase with the Sekimeiya has disappeared.
Katei chases a sound out of the storeroom. In hallway A, he sees Naomi with the suitcase and chases after her.
Running up the floors, Katei trips on the third set of stairs. Realizing that he will be unable to enter the attic, he returns to the crystal floor to assess the situation.

-Crystal room B4
The cabinet where the Sekimeiya was first hidden on that day is set to 0ºC, and the temperature wheel is not broken. I lift the cover, and we see the Sekimeiya inside the cabinet.
The Sekimeiya is burning hot, so we take it out of the cabinet and touch it, hoping to escape from the tower. When I make contact with it, the Sekimeiya disappears, and Shiroya soon notices that the cabinet closed without making a noise.
-Hallway B
We step out of the room when we hear someone running through the hallway. We can't see anyone, but we follow the steps up the tower.
-Floor 6
We hear the attic door being shut, and it's locked when we reach it. Shiroya takes out the attic key from her purse and unlocks the door.
-Attic
After Shiroya peeks into the living room, she disappears.

-Ashiya Tower
I enter the tower early in the morning through the storeroom. With the duct tape, I cover a camera in hallway B. I make it to the security room before the smoke is released. I can see Miiya through the monitors.
After the smoke is released, I uncover the camera and record Akaro and Katei's secret movements. I save the recording on the USB drive and leave the room before Katei can see me.
I follow behind the group to learn their movements.
Miiya sees me from the event room, and I have to act as the Atsuki from this world until he returns with Sai.
A long time passes while Akaro and Sai repeatedly find and hide the Sekimeiya.
The other Atsuki and Miiya return from the attic. I hide in room A1 so that I'm not seen, and I hear Suripo's voice from inside. A while later, the group finds him dead in the lobby.
The group begins to search through the building. When my other self enters room A1, I tell him to stay there while I search through the other rooms, not revealing all the Sekimeiya. Miiya and I search through the other floors and can't find anyone. Meanwhile, the group finds the storeroom's secret after my past self leaves it.
When we return to the crystal floor, Miiya goes to the storeroom and is eventually joined by my other self. The entire group goes to the attic and eventually disappears from the building, leaving my past self experimenting with the Sekimeiya.
